name: Collect owner payments
summary: After a monthly progress draw is certified, the contractor's billing and collections specialists make sure the owner pays it. They track the 14-day notice and 28-day payment dates, load invoices into owner portals, chase late payments, involve the project manager and finance manager for disputes and old balances, apply receipts and tell accounts payable so subcontractors are paid within 7 days. Slow public approvals, owner disputes and short payments stretch working capital and can push disputes to adjudication.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 220 active projects, a central billing and collections team in finance transactions and regional finance managers.
baseline.notes: Ontario prompt payment applied to contracts entered after 1 October 2019; older contracts and other provinces paid under contract terms (often 30 days after certification). The share of contracts under the new rules grew through 2020-2022.

unit_of_work: one certified progress draw (or holdback invoice) collected
trigger: The project accountant hands over a certified progress draw or holdback invoice for collection.
end_state: The owner's payment is applied to the invoice, AP has been told so subcontractors can be paid, and the entries are posted.

volume.seasonality: Steady through the year; collections slow over the December holidays and around public owners' 31 March fiscal year-end approvals.

evidence.note: About 220 progress draws plus about 15 holdback invoices a month, from the organisation file's volumes.

systems.name: Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)

steps.name: Log the certified draw in the collections tracker
steps.description: The billing and collections specialist opens the certified draw handed over by the project accountant, enters the invoice, certified amount, holdback and delivery date in the receivables tracker, and diarises day 14 and day 28 under the prompt payment rules or the contract's payment date.

error.defect_description: Due date diarised from the certificate date instead of the invoice delivery date.

evidence.note: 28-day payment and 14-day notice periods run from delivery of the proper invoice.

steps.name: Confirm the owner received the invoice
steps.description: The billing specialist checks the owner's acknowledgement email or portal status and, for owners that pay through a supplier portal, checks whether the invoice still has to be loaded there with a purchase order number.

next.condition: owner pays through a supplier portal
invoice accepted by email or paper

evidence.note: Share of public and institutional owners using supplier portals is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load the invoice into the owner's supplier portal
steps.description: For hospitals, universities and other owners with supplier portals, the billing specialist re-keys the invoice header, purchase order, amount, holdback and tax into the portal and uploads the application, certificate and statutory declaration as PDFs.

error.defect_description: Wrong PO line or amount, so the portal rejects the invoice.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of owner portal practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait out the owner's notice period
steps.description: The owner's accounts payable and project staff review the invoice; under Ontario's prompt payment rules they must give a notice of non-payment within 14 days of the proper invoice if they dispute any part of it.

next.condition: notice of non-payment for part or all of the invoice

evidence.note: 14-day notice of non-payment rule; the remaining wait is short because certification already used part of the period. Share of invoices with a notice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Log the notice of non-payment and alert AP
steps.description: The billing specialist records the disputed amount and the owner's reasons, sends the notice to the project manager and to accounts payable the same day so that matching notices can go to affected subcontractors within the 7-day window.

error.defect_description: Alert reaches AP too late for the subcontractor notice deadline.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act s. 6.5: contractor notice to subcontractors within 7 days of the owner's notice

evidence.note: Contractor's notice deadline is the earlier of 7 days after the owner's notice or 35 days after the invoice.

steps.name: Decide how to answer the dispute
steps.description: The project manager reads the owner's reasons, checks the work and change records, and decides whether to accept the reduction and re-bill it, negotiate it at the next owner meeting, or refer it to adjudication through legal.

next.condition: accept or negotiate; undisputed balance still due

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimates; adjudication was new in Ontario from October 2019 and used sparingly in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve referral to adjudication
steps.description: The regional finance manager reviews the disputed amount and the project manager's case, approves the referral and the undertaking to adjudicate given to subcontractors, and passes the file to legal for the notice of adjudication.
outputs: notice of non-payment file to legal

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act: undertaking to refer the owner's non-payment to adjudication within 21 days

evidence.note: 21-day undertaking; adjudicator decides within 30 days and payment follows within 10 days.

steps.name: Wait for the payment due date
steps.description: The owner's payment run processes approved invoices; most public owners pay in a weekly or bi-weekly cheque or EFT run close to the due date, while some private owners wait for their own lender's funding.

next.condition: not received by the due date

evidence.note: Share paid on time is the author's estimate: Ontario's 28-day rule shortened public owner payment but late payment stayed common.

steps.name: Chase the overdue payment
steps.description: The billing specialist phones and emails the owner's accounts payable, checks the portal for holds or rejections, resends any missing document and records the promised payment date in the tracker.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Escalate with the owner's project representative
steps.description: The project manager raises the unpaid draw with the owner's project representative at the site meeting or by phone, finds out whether the delay is funding, approvals or a hidden dispute, and asks for a payment date in writing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the aged draw and approve a demand
steps.description: At the monthly aged receivables review the regional finance manager looks at draws more than 45 to 60 days old, decides whether to send a formal demand with interest under the contract or Act, and whether to warn of suspension or lien rights.

control.basis: Credit policy: finance approval before formal demand, interest or suspension notice to an owner

evidence.note: Monthly aged-receivable review is common finance practice; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the owner to pay after the demand
steps.description: The owner pays after the demand, after its funding arrives or after the dispute settles; a few cases move to adjudication or lien proceedings handled by legal, and the draw is collected when that ends.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Import the bank receipt
steps.description: The bank's EFT and lockbox file is imported into the ERP cash module overnight, creating an unapplied receipt with the owner's remittance reference for the billing specialist to match.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 bank integration.

steps.name: Apply the receipt to the invoice
steps.description: The billing specialist matches the remittance advice to the invoice, applies the cash in the ERP receivables ledger, and checks whether the amount equals the certified amount less holdback.

error.defect_description: Receipt applied to the wrong project's invoice.

evidence.note: Share of short payments is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate a short payment
steps.description: The billing specialist works out why the owner paid less, such as extra holdback, a backcharge, a tax error or a missed change order, confirms with the owner and the project manager, and either rebills or chases the balance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Tell AP the owner has paid
steps.description: The billing specialist emails accounts payable and the project accountant that payment for this draw has arrived, with the date and amount, because subcontractors included in the draw must be paid within 7 days of that receipt.

error.defect_description: AP not told, so subcontractor payment misses the 7-day deadline.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act s. 6.5: pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment

steps.name: Update the holdback ledger
steps.description: The project accountant updates the project's holdback ledger with the holdback retained on this draw, so owner holdback receivable and subcontractor holdback payable can be compared at substantial performance.

error.defect_description: Holdback recorded at the wrong amount.

evidence.note: Holdback tracked until release; ledger practice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Report the receipt to treasury
steps.description: The billing specialist adds the receipt to the daily cash report that treasury uses for the weekly cash forecast and the revolving credit draw, with expected receipts for the coming weeks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Post receivable journal entries
steps.description: The ERP posts the cash and receivable entries to the general ledger and the receivable drops off the aged report; month-end receivable balances flow to the close without further handling.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Owner notice of non-payment
exceptions.description: The owner disputes part of the invoice within 14 days; AP must notify affected trades within 7 days and the PM decides whether to negotiate or adjudicate.

exceptions.name: Referral to adjudication
exceptions.description: The finance manager approves an undertaking to adjudicate and legal takes the dispute to ODACC.

exceptions.name: Late payment escalated
exceptions.description: A chase does not produce payment and the PM escalates with the owner's representative.

exceptions.name: Aged draw with formal demand
exceptions.description: Draws more than 45 to 60 days old get a finance-approved demand and wait for funding or settlement.

exceptions.name: Short payment
exceptions.description: The owner pays less than certified and the specialist investigates and rebills or chases.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the certified draw reaching collections to cash applied
benchmarks.population: Progress draws of Canadian building contractors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: a proper invoice is due 28 days after delivery and certification takes about a week, so an on-time payment arrives about 20 days after handover; late payers extend the tail.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from proper invoice to payment

pain_points.description: Owner supplier portals need the invoice re-keyed with purchase order lines and reject small mismatches.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: The 7-day subcontractor deadlines depend on AP hearing promptly about owner notices and receipts, which happens by email.

evidence.note: Deadlines from the Act; email handoff is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Late payers take repeated chasing and PM escalation, which uses project time and leaves cash tied up.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (1.35 loading on salaried wages).
The project accountant is included for the holdback ledger update; the organisation file lists only the billing specialist, PM and finance manager on this process.
P3 Project Co payments are added as an input and holdback invoices as a trigger; the organisation file lacks both links.
The owner portal step uses the government portals system id as the closest system in the organisation file.

Hands-on time is only about 1.7 hours per draw, so the process uses about 3.9 FTE; the organisation file's 10 billing specialists also bill holdback, handle change order invoices, credit checks and month-end receivable reporting.

The simulated median cycle time (21.0 days) matches the 22-day estimate; the simulated p90 (33.2 days) is shorter than the 50-day estimate because a few disputed or unfunded draws wait months, a tail the triangular waits do not reach.

sources.title: Prompt Payment for Construction in Ontario
sources.supports: Construction Act Part I.1 in force 1 October 2019 for contracts entered after that date; proper invoice monthly unless the contract says otherwise and cannot depend on certifier action; owner pays within 28 days; owner notice of non-payment within 14 days; contractor pays subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment, or 35 days after the proper invoice unless it gives notice; undertaking to adjudicate within 21 days.

sources.title: Prompt payment and adjudication have arrived in Ontario
sources.supports: Holdback release mandatory unless the payer publishes a notice of non-payment of holdback; annual or phased release allowed with contract provisions; holdback may be secured by letter of credit or bond; lien preservation 60 days and perfection 90 days; adjudicator decision within 30 days; payment within 10 days of a determination.
